question.problem:
Suppose that $f(x,y)$ is a differentiable function such that

$$
f(3,-1)=-3,\,{f}_{x}(3,-1)=-1,\,{f}_{y}(3,-1)=1.
$$

Using a linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(3,-1),$ estimate the value of $f(3.01,-0.97).$
question.worked_solution:
The linear approximation of the function $f$ at the point $(a,b)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y)≈f(a,b)+∇f(a,b)\cdot ⟨x-a,y-b⟩.
$$

So, the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(3,-1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ≈f(3,-1)+∇f(3,-1)\cdot ⟨x-3,y+1⟩ \\  & =f(3,-1)+⟨{f}_{x}(3,-1),{f}_{y}(3,-1)⟩\cdot ⟨x-3,y+1⟩ \\  & =-3+⟨-1,1⟩\cdot ⟨x-3,y+1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We can approximate $f(3.01,-0.97)$ by evaluating the linear approximation at $x=3.01$ and $y=-0.97,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(3.01,-0.97) & ≈-3+⟨-1,1⟩\cdot ⟨3.01-3,-0.97+1⟩ \\  & =-3+⟨-1,1⟩\cdot ⟨0.01,0.03⟩ \\  & =-3-0.01+0.03 \\  & =-2.98\end{aligned}
$$
